title: These Cats and Dogs Have the Best Job Ever: Taste-Testing Pet Food for a $17 Billion Industry
summary:
At a Royal Canin research center, about 160 of them are tasked with taste-testing pet food while nutritionists document their preferences, behavior and stool quality.
The goal is to develop premium blends that satisfy both the animal’s taste buds and the owner’s parental instincts.
Americans spent more than $17 billion on cat food over the last year, up 14% from two years earlier, according to The New York Times.
The pet food industry has kept growing despite inflation, and companies are rolling out premium lines for wealthier customers as the K-shaped economy persists.
Their taste buds also fade over time, but their sense of bitterness doesn’t.

title: Gen X is going deeper into credit card debt — even as they make more money than ever
summary:
Gen Xers are putting their credit cards to work.
The Federal Reserve's latest accounting of consumer finances finds that as of 2025, 45 to 54-year-olds had the largest credit card balances among age groups, surpassing 64 to 75-year-olds.
At the same time, their younger millennial peers have been paying down debt, with balances for 35 to 44-year-olds falling.
Their older peers' median assets, which include things like stocks, bonds, and retirement accounts, have risen since 2022, bolstering their net worths.
Are you a Gen Xer struggling with rising costs or credit card balances?

title: She Grew Up on Food Stamps and Started a Hedge Fund at MIT. Now Her 8-Figure Startup Counts Nvidia and OpenAI as Clients.
summary:
Listen to this postKey Takeaways Christina Qi started a hedge fund as an undergraduate at MIT, building it to trade $7 billion per day.
A “really bad year in 2020” caused the hedge fund to shut down.
As a 21-year-old undergraduate at MIT, she quietly did something most finance veterans spend decades attempting: She started her own hedge fund.
At its height, the fund, Domeyard, traded $7 billion in volume per day.
In 2020, after eight years of running Domeyard, Qi and her fellow founding partners realized that the fund was not scalable, and performance was suffering.

title: Mac Shipments Fall, But Apple Still Gains Ground in Shrinking Market
summary:
Apple's Mac shipments declined 11.3% in the third quarter of 2026, but the company increased its market share as worldwide PC shipments fell more sharply, according to IDC's latest preliminary estimates.
That put Apple's market share at 9.5%, up from 8.5% in the third quarter of 2025.
Across all brands, shipments dropped to 62.7 million units from 78.5 million a year earlier, a decline of 20.1%.
Lenovo led the market with 14.9 million shipments, followed by HP with 10.3 million and Dell with 7.6 million.
ASUS, in fifth place with 5.5 million shipments, recorded an 8.6% decrease, making it the only top-five vendor with a smaller percentage decline than Apple.

title: EA reportedly leans on a private rating as bondholders claim default
summary:
Electronic Arts has told creditors it holds an investment-grade rating for some of its bonds, and is using it to argue it owes them nothing after going private.
Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund, Silver Lake and Jared Kushner’s Affinity Partners took EA private on 4 August for $55B, the largest leveraged buyout on record.
Holders can demand 101 cents if a change of control coincides with a loss of investment grade.
Fitch withdrew its investment-grade rating in late June.
The creditors, advised by Akin Gump and Houlihan Lokey, say a private grade cannot replace a public one.
